title: S3 industrial site with local authority and bounded upstream independence

scope.description: Fictional Quarry site requires up to 24 hours of bounded local identity, authorization, security evidence, communications and recovery during upstream loss. Safety decisions remain with a local safety authority. The delivery contains only a small local software model; no industrial platform or physical process is deployed or exercised.
outOfScope: Physical actuation, PLC/SCADA writes or safety-interlock changes
Actual AD/AD FS, Entra, Azure Local or Azure Stack Hub behavior
Network interruption, billable resources or 24-hour endurance tests
assumptions: The local safety owner must approve actual maximum duration, safe state and restart criteria before any real test.
Corporate compromise or unavailability must not grant or deny required local operating authority.
Local hardware/power, identity, policy, keys, time, DNS, PKI, evidence and communications must each have an independently operable implementation.
S3 is a connectivity/continuity requirement, not a command to add an Entra tenant or a proof of product eligibility.

requirements.text: Authenticate approved local operators and enforce local roles for up to 24 hours of upstream loss without Entra/corporate runtime authorization; deny central-only identities and unknown/expired/revoked local credentials.
acceptance: Local issuer/audience/expiry/revocation enforcement demonstrated on the actual selected identity stack.
Local session lifetime no more than 15 minutes; local reauthentication only while all autonomy prerequisites remain valid.
Corporate credentials cannot become local administrative credentials.
unknowns: Actual local identity system, custody, revocation and runtime independence untested.

requirements.text: Local approved policy permits only declared operational functions; the supplied model permits synthetic telemetry read and alarm acknowledgement and denies all physical actuation.
acceptance: Locally approved version is used when upstream policy is unavailable.
Unlisted actions, central-only roles and physical commands deny.
Policy/deployment identity cannot grant itself safety authority.
unknowns: Actual enforcement points and legacy-device compensating controls require a hazard-approved test.

requirements.text: A local safety authority can stop operation and veto restart independently of central cybersecurity commands; restart requires local safety and recovery approval after prerequisites and revocations are reconciled.
acceptance: Signed site hazard/safe-state/restart analysis and authority matrix.
No cyber operator or central-only identity bypasses safety veto.
Actual interlocks remain independent and are never bypassed by this exercise.
unknowns: No real safety authority approval, hazard review or physical safe-state observation exists.

requirements.text: Retain local security evidence for the 24-hour window at a synthetic peak of ten 1-KiB events/minute with 2x reserve; allocate at least 64 MiB plus independently justified overhead and protect provenance/access/export.
acceptance: 14,400 events/day × 1 KiB × 2 = 28.125 MiB before overhead, within the proposed 64-MiB reserve.
Loss of central ingestion does not disable local detection.
Evidence capacity/integrity failure leads to approved restricted/safe state without silent discard.
unknowns: Real event rate, durable storage, integrity anchor, detection and retention not tested; the model uses only a 32-event queue.

requirements.text: Local keys, approved name records, time and PKI/revocation material remain usable through the window; local session/signing trust is limited and cloud key retrieval is not required.
acceptance: Declared clock error bound 60 seconds; exceeding it blocks operations.
Name/trust/key failures individually trigger the approved restricted/safe state.
Proposed signing/PKI validity is 48 hours and revocation material at least 24 hours; actual root/renewal/holdover and expiry tests required.
unknowns: DNS, time, PKI, key protection, revocation delivery, power and renewal are model flags, not actual services.

requirements.text: Local operators and safety staff retain an approved two-way local alarm/coordination channel; central SIEM/ITSM unavailability cannot gate time-critical response.
acceptance: Send and acknowledgement observed on actual local communications.
Required communications loss leads to approved safe behavior.
Incident evidence is reconciled later without a ticketing dependency.
unknowns: In-memory mailbox tests do not validate actual radio, intercom, delivery or staffing.

requirements.text: At 24 hours, credential expiry or loss of a mandatory local dependency, stop new privileged/state-changing work and enter the site-approved safe state; no silent extension or fail-open.
acceptance: Boundary tests at/after expiry and autonomy maximum.
One-fault-at-a-time key, time, DNS, PKI, communications and evidence-capacity behavior.
Actual real-duration endurance and hazard-approved safe-state execution before operation.
unknowns: Accelerated logical clock is not real 24-hour endurance or physical shutdown proof.

requirements.text: Recover local identity/policy/evidence from independently custodied offline state within two hours with a 24-hour baseline RPO, without an Entra-only vault, online certificate renewal or cloud recovery authorization.
acceptance: Independent media, local keys, time/DNS/PKI and protected recovery console are reachable.
Known-good object/role/policy relationships and revocations are reconciled.
Restore measured on the selected actual platform with safety authority present.
unknowns: No hardware, power, actual backup restore, RTO/RPO or platform eligibility validation.

requirements.text: On upstream return, retain and reconcile local logs, revocations and policy versions before approved resumption; do not overwrite local safety decisions or re-enable stale identities.
acceptance: Local ordered evidence survives modeled export until receipt acknowledged.
Revoked local identity remains denied after reconnect.
Actual upstream ingestion and conflict resolution separately tested.
unknowns: No live ingestion, policy reconciliation or cross-system authority conflict tested.

boundaries.crossingRule: Corporate tenant is not the local runtime identity or safety authority; product-specific deployment choice is unresolved.

Central observations cannot grant local operating/recovery or safety rights.
Site-specific law/hazard analysis and cryptographic/operator authority need explicit sign-off.
Retain raw evidence locally; export only approved fields with receipt and integrity reconciliation.
The fixture changes an in-memory flag only; any real disconnection or segmentation test needs a separate safety-approved lab.
Local services enforce purpose-specific rights and fail behavior; cloud inventory/management is not runtime control.
Cybersecurity actions never override local safety veto or interlocks; no physical operation is authorized here.
